newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AUTO SLOWDOWN DENTS SOUTH AFRICAN Q3 MANUFACTURING.
newsitem.headline: AUTO SLOWDOWN DENTS SOUTH AFRICAN Q3 MANUFACTURING.

text.p: A sharp slowdown in motor industry production in the face of rising imports was a key contributor to a fall in South African manufacturing output in the third quarter, the Central Statistical Service said.

Manufacturing production in the three months to end-September was 0.7 percent lower than the year ago period, despite rapid growth of 46.2 percent in the non-ferrous metal industry and stable petroleum industry output.
Production in the motor vehicle industry fell by 11.8 percent, despite a rise in new vehicle sales of approximately eight percent.
The CSS said the discrepancy between output and sales reflected a considerable increase in the number of vehicles sold with no or a relatively low local content.
The National Association of Automative Component and Allied Manufacturers (NAACAM) said earlier this month that reduced import duties had triggered a sharp rise in car imports.
NAACAM president Johan Meyer said South Africa was importing about 30,000 fully built-up vehicles a year. That compares with total new vehicle sales in the first 10 months of 1996 of 330,291.

The 0.7 percentage point decrease in manufacturing production in the third quarter was mainly the result of low motor industry output (which contributed -0.8 percentage point), iron and steel (-0.7), clothing (-0.5) and paper (-0.5).
These decreases were counteracted by higher production in basic non-ferrous metals (+1.0), food (+0.6) and machinery and equipment (+0.5).
The fall in output was particulary sharp in September when manufacuring production fell 1.8 percent year-on-year on a seasonally-adjusted basis, and 3.0 percent month-on-month.
